name: verus-constraints
description: "Mandatory rules for writing Verus code. Covers verus! block syntax, source integrity for exec code, forbidden patterns, and assume_specification policy. Must be followed whenever producing or modifying Verus-annotated code."
---

# Verus Constraints

Study `docs/examples/binary-search/proof/` for a complete example following all
constraints below.

## verus! { } Blocks Only

All spec and proof code **must** use native `verus! { }` block syntax.
Do **not** use attribute-based syntax (`#[verus_spec]`, `#[verus_verify]`, `proof! { }`).

```rust
// ✅ CORRECT
verus! {
    fn foo(x: u32) -> (ret: u32)
        requires x < 100,
        ensures ret == x + 1,
    { x + 1 }
} // verus!

// ❌ WRONG — attribute style
#[verus_spec(ret => requires x < 100, ensures ret == x + 1)]
fn foo(x: u32) -> u32 { x + 1 }
```

Even if existing code uses attribute style, write all new code in `verus! { }` style.
Attribute style is less mature; `verus! { }` can be auto-converted later.

## Source Integrity (exec code)

The following rules apply to the original source files (e.g. `lib.rs`), not to
`*.spec.rs` / `*.proof.rs` which are freely editable.

Verus verification is **in-place**: specs and proofs are added directly alongside
exec code. The annotated code remains fully compilable and runnable — Verus
constructs are erased during normal `cargo build` via cfg-gating. Do not change
code logic; keep changes minimal so developers can review diffs easily.

**Preserve:** exec logic, function signatures, struct definitions, comments,
debug assertions, and all other existing code. If a construct is unsupported by
Verus (e.g. `debug_assert!`), cfg-gate it with `#[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]`
rather than deleting.

**Allowed additions:** `verus! { }` blocks (requires, ensures, invariants, decreases,
proof blocks, assert), vstd imports (cfg-gated), named returns `-> (ret: T)`,
ghost/tracked variables, `#[cfg_attr(not(verus_keep_ghost), derive(...))]` gating.

**Never change:** semantic code logic or function/struct signatures. Exception:
only if Verus genuinely cannot express a construct — first search vstd for
alternatives, build a minimal reproducer proving unsupported, then make the
smallest change needed and document why.

**Iterator rewrite rule:** When exec code uses Iterator chains
(`.iter().filter().map().collect()`), these MUST be rewritten to while
loops because Iterator API is unsupported. This is a permitted exec
change because: (1) the behavioral semantics are identical, (2) it is
a true Verus limitation, (3) the ensures should describe the ORIGINAL
functional intent using `Seq::filter`/`Seq::map_values`, not the
rewritten loop structure.

**After completing all changes**, use the `ast-consistency` skill to verify
source integrity. Fix all inconsistencies. For unavoidable ones, you must
confirm: (1) the code still builds with `cargo build`, (2) semantic code logic
is unchanged, (3) it is a genuine Verus limitation, and (4) it is documented.

## Forbidden Patterns

| Pattern | Policy |
|---|---|
| `admit()` | Banned — only as placeholder in initial skeleton proofs |
| `assume(...)` | Banned |
| `#[verifier::external_body]` | Banned **as a workaround** for spec/proof difficulty. Permitted ONLY for functions that use a True Limitation feature (async, float arithmetic, transmute, static mut) — see True Limitations table below. If the function body is pure Rust with supported types, it MUST be verified, not escaped. |
| `#[verifier::trusted]` | Banned |
| `#[verifier::external]` | Banned — do not use to "fix" verification errors |
| `#[verifier::exec_allows_no_decreases_clause]` | Banned |
| `#[verifier::rlimit(N)]` | Timeout means the proof is too weak — simplify the proof, split lemmas, add intermediate assertions. Never use rlimit to work around timeouts. If all proof strategies are exhausted and the proof is genuinely optimal, rlimit up to 50 is the absolute maximum |

## assume_specification — Human-Approved Only

`assume_specification` and `axiom` are **external-bottom** trust
assumptions (see **spec-design** skill, Part 2). They introduce
unverified axioms — if wrong, the entire verification is unsound.

`external_type_specification` is safe to use freely — it only declares
that a type exists without introducing logical assumptions.

**You must NOT write `assume_specification` or `axiom` yourself** unless
a human has explicitly approved them (e.g., via checked items in the
property analysis). If you discover a missing assumption, report it and
use `admit()` as a temporary placeholder.

**Before reporting:** search vstd for existing specs of that function,
look for safe Verus API alternatives, try restructuring to avoid the call.

## vstd & Common Misconceptions

Before writing custom specs, search vstd for existing ones (sequences, sets,
maps, arithmetic, pointers, atomics).

- **Never invent vstd functions** — verify existence in actual vstd source.
- **Verus supports `for` loops** — do not replace with `while` unless semantically appropriate.
- **Don't hallucinate syntax** — when unsure, check the Verus reference or vstd examples.

## False Limitations (v0.2026.04.03)

The following features **work** in current Verus. Do NOT claim they are unsupported:

| Feature | Status | Notes |
|---------|--------|-------|
| `dyn trait` (basic + Box\<dyn\>) | ✅ Works | Including trait with spec methods |
| `DerefMut` / `v[i] = x` on `&mut Vec` | ✅ Works | Use `v.set(i, x)` |
| Multiple `&mut` params (`swap(a, b)`) | ✅ Works | `old(a)`, `old(b)` in ensures |
| `std::collections::HashMap` (basic) | ✅ Works | `new()`, `insert()` verified |
| `Box::new` with ensures | ✅ Works | `ensures *b == 42` |
| `Option::unwrap_or` | ✅ Works | |
| Nested `proof fn` calls (3+ layers) | ✅ Works | |
| `for` loop with `iter:` | ✅ Works | |
| `const fn` | ✅ Works | Needs overflow handling |
| Recursive types (`Box<Self>`) | ✅ Works | Add `decreases self` |
| `type_invariant` | ✅ Works | Use `proof { use_type_invariant(self); }` |
| `broadcast proof/use` | ✅ Works | |
| `Seq::filter` / `Seq::map_values` in spec | ✅ Works | Exec needs loop, but spec can use these |

## Spec Vocabulary Reference

When writing spec, you have these tools. Each includes **when to use** (not just what it is):

**choose:** `choose|x: T| P(x)` — Use when you have `exists|x| P(x)` and need a concrete witness value in a spec expression. Without this, you cannot define spec functions that "pick" a satisfying element.

**Extensional equality:** `=~=` for Seq/Set/Map, `=~~=` for nested collections. In many simple cases `==` also works for Seq, but when Z3 struggles with collection equality, switch to `=~=`. **Guideline: start with `==`, use `=~=` if Z3 can't prove it.**

**old():** `old(self)@` in ensures of `&mut` functions. **Test: does this function take &mut? Then ensures MUST contain old().** Without this, ensures compares new state to itself (tautological).

**ghost struct:** Use when you need a spec-only abstraction that has no exec counterpart. Example: an `Interval { lo: int, hi: int }` for reasoning about address ranges that don't exist as a runtime type.

**spec_fn:** `spec_fn(T) -> U` — Use when a spec needs to be parameterized by a function. Example: a generic "map" spec that takes a transformation function.

**Seq operations in spec:** Even though `Iterator` chains are not available in exec, `Seq` provides the same operations in spec: `s.filter(|x| p(x))`, `s.map_values(|x| f(x))`, `s.subrange(lo, hi)`, `s.update(i, x)`, `s.contains(x)`. **When exec uses a while loop to implement filter/map, the ensures should still use Seq::filter/map_values to express the intent declaratively.**

**Map::dom():** Returns `Set<K>`. Use for "all keys satisfy P": `forall|k| m.dom().contains(k) ==> P(m[k])`. Without this, you can't quantify over Map keys.

## True Limitations (cannot work around in spec)

| Feature | Impact on Spec |
|---------|---------------|
| `async fn` / `await` | Cannot write requires/ensures. Must use `#[verifier::external]`. |
| `f32`/`f64` arithmetic in spec | Cannot reason about float results. |
| `static mut` | No spec model. |
| `transmute` | No spec model. |
